business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Desktop 3D Printers and Resin Filaments

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620–763 on the Aktiengesellschaft; registration duty under Art. 640 OR; articles of association and incorporation deed formalities under Arts. 626 and 629 OR; audit opt-out under Art. 727a OR; beneficial owner disclosure under Art. 934o OR.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) of the canton of the registered office, with federal coordination by the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office (EHRA) in Bern; electronic filing through the federal eChange portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial incorporation deed (Errichtungsurkunde) with certified Articles of Association (Statuten), submitted electronically via eChange and published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Articles must state a nominal share capital of at least CHF 100,000; before registration at least 20% (CHF 20,000) must be paid in cash and deposited into a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a licensed Swiss bank; the escrow confirmation must accompany the registration application; contributions in kind must be fully paid in and substantiated in an incorporation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the first meeting of the Board of Directors of the Company: 1. Subscription of 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 par value each, constituting the full CHF 100,000 share capital, is accepted, and the mandatory CHF 20,000 cash payment into a blocked escrow account at a Swiss bank is confirmed. 2. The registered office is fixed at Rue du Commerce 12, Geneva, Switzerland. 3. [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name] is appointed Head of Finance, each with dual-signature authority. 4. The incorporation deed and Articles of Association are ratified, and the application to the Swiss Commercial Register is authorized. 5. Formation expenses are approved as presented.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Association and Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (Notariat) of the canton of the registered office, acting under Arts. 626 and 629 of the Swiss Code of Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association specifying the corporate name, purpose (online retail of 3D printers and consumables, ISIC 4791), registered office, share capital structure, board composition, and publication method. All founders must personally appear before the notary, sign the deed, and have the notary certify the authenticated copy for the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or identity card of each founder
Draft Articles of Association (German/French with English translation if desired)
Founder register showing share allocations and payments
Power of attorney for each representative acting on behalf of a founder
Beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires amendments, revise the clauses to conform to mandatory provisions of the Swiss Code of Obligations and re-sign the deed; if a founder refuses to sign, substitute a new founder and re-execute before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Minimum Paid-Up Capital into a Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank or fiduciary escrow provider (e.g., UBS, ZKB, or a formation-specialized fintech offering Sperrkonto services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the name of the company to be formed; deposit at least CHF 20,000, representing 20% of the CHF 100,000 nominal capital; obtain a written escrow confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) stating the depositor, amount, and blocking condition; the funds remain blocked until the Commercial Register issues the registration certificate, at which point the company may release them.
required_dossiers: Extract of the notarized incorporation deed
Beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declaration under Swiss anti-money laundering rules (GwG)
Swiss bank account opening and escrow forms
Draft Articles of Association for reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds, provide bank references, audited financial statements, or contractual evidence of lawful origin; if the escrow confirmation contains errors, request a corrected statement; alternatively, transfer the mandate to another licensed bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Registration Application with the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) via the federal eChange electronic platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the eChange application attaching the notarized incorporation deed, Articles of Association, list of directors and authorized signatories with specimen signatures, auditor opt-out or consent, and the beneficial owner registry; pay the cantonal and federal registration fees; the registrar verifies legal compliance under Art. 640 OR and issues the Certificate of Registration (Handelsregisterauszug).
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation deed and Articles of Association (authenticated copy)
eChange application form bearing qualified electronic signatures of the directors
List of directors and authorized signatories with specimen signatures
Audit opt-out declaration under Art. 727a OR or the appointed auditor's written consent
Beneficial owner registry under Art. 934o OR
Escrow account confirmation from the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a deficiency letter (Mängelrüge), cure the defects within the stated deadline (normally 30 days) by resubmitting corrected declarations; a refusal can be appealed to the cantonal supervisory authority (Aufsichtsbehörde) within 10 days of written notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce and Effectiveness Against Third Parties
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt - SHAB), operated under the direction of the Federal Commercial Register Office (EHRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the Commercial Register automatically transmits the legal announcement to SHAB; verify the published corporate name, purpose, capital, and directors; the company acquires legal personality upon registration, but the content becomes effective against third parties upon SHAB publication.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register registration number and Certificate of Registration
Approved text of corporate purpose and capital for publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB publication contains factual errors regarding the purpose, capital, or officers, file a correction request with the Commercial Register; the rectification will be published as a formal amendment without penalty if raised promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT Registration and Operational Notifications Prior to Commencement of Online Sales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung - ESTV/FTA), VAT Division; cantonal economic affairs and labor offices for confirmatory notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for VAT through the Swiss e-service portal if projected taxable turnover from the online store exceeds CHF 100,000 per year; obtain the company's UID number (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) shown on the Commercial Register extract; file the opening declaration; no separate trade license is required for pure e-commerce retail, but the online shop must display the full company identification and registered office.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register Certificate of Registration
UID number and company identification data
Estimated annual turnover declaration
Online shop imprint and terms of sale draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is delayed, file an ex-post registration request and settle any back-dated VAT within the statutory limitation period; if customs or chemicals authorities query the resin imports, provide the Safety Data Sheets and the Swiss importer declaration to the Federal Customs Administration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure online retail under ISIC 4791. The distribution of chemical consumer goods (resin filaments and 3D printer consumables) is supervised by the Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt für Umwelt - BAFU) and the cantonal chemicals inspectorate, not by an industrial licensing board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operational manufacturing or industrial operating permit is required for online retail of 3D printers and consumables; a general business notification to the cantonal economic office and, where applicable, a warehouse occupancy permit from the municipal building authority are sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt für Umwelt - BAFU) and the competent cantonal environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from formal EIA under Annex 10 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV), as retail and warehousing activities are not listed as EIA projects. However, the placing of resin consumables on the market triggers a chemical notification duty under Art. 5 of the Chemicals Ordinance (ChemRRV), and the retail operator must appoint a Swiss-based person responsible for placing chemicals on the market.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater or point-source emissions arise from warehousing and logistics. Workplace VOC concentrations must stay below Swiss MAK/TLV values (e.g., ≤ 20 ppm for methyl methacrylate and ≤ 50 ppm for styrene vapors per SUVA guidance). Resin storage must be in ventilated, climate-controlled cabinets; waste resins and contaminated packaging are classified as hazardous waste under the Waste Ordinance (VVEA) and must be removed by a licensed disposal contractor. Safety Data Sheets under the Swiss Chemicals Ordinance must accompany all dangerous resin products at first delivery.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety acceptance certificate (Feuerpolizeiliche Abnahmebescheinigung) issued by the cantonal fire prevention authority in accordance with VKF guidelines; structural load inspection and building clearance for warehouse racking; occupational safety inspection by SUVA confirming safe manual handling of filament spools, sealed chemical storage lockers, emergency eyewash stations, and first-aid equipment under Ordinance 3 on Occupational Health and Safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni ATC); official portal for VAT registration and filing: Swiss Federal Tax Administration VAT e-services (www.estv.admin.ch)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Swiss AGs automatically receive a UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) from the Swiss Federal Statistical Office upon commercial register entry; the UID serves as the VAT number. Foreign entities not domiciled in Switzerland must mandatory register for Swiss VAT with ESTV if performing taxable supplies in Switzerland, irrespective of turnover, and must submit an online application (or written application) including company excerpt, certificate of incorporation, board/power of attorney, and a designated Swiss fiscal representative (if required). The ESTV then assigns a Swiss VAT number (MWST-Nr.), typically congruent with the UID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.territorial_scope: Swiss VAT applies to supplies of goods and services rendered in Switzerland by resident and non-resident enterprises; supplies by Swiss enterprises to foreign recipients are generally outside the territorial scope or zero-rated if export conditions are met.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_exempt_zone_status: None; Switzerland is a customs and VAT territory with no general free-trade-zone VAT exemption. (Selected free zones, e.g. Geneva and Chiasso, apply only to non-VAT warehousing procedures; no corporate income tax holiday.)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: VAT group election under Art. 15 LTVA allows closely linked Swiss enterprises to be treated as one VAT person. Small business election (Art. 11 LTVA) permits exemption for turnover under CHF 100,000. No US-style check-the-box election exists in Switzerland. For direct taxes, hybrid entity classification follows the Swiss legal classification under Art. 50 LIFD; special mixed-status foreign entities are reclassified under Swiss domestic law, and hybrid mismatch rules under Art. 61a LTVA apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover for Swiss-domiciled legal entities; non-established foreign legal persons have no registration threshold and must register for VAT upon first taxable supply in Switzerland
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time fiscal clearance, API field-level tax control, or digital stamping regime. Electronic invoicing (Peppol, eBill, PDF) is permitted provided the invoice satisfies the content requirements of Art. 26 LTVA (vendor, recipient, description, consideration, date, separate VAT rate/amount). Tax authorities may require digital submission via the Swiss VAT system (eVI), but there is no per-invoice pre-clearance approval.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to foreign destinations qualify for zero-rating (0% VAT) under Art. 6 para 1 lit a LTVA if the goods are physically transported out of Switzerland by the supplier or a third party. Services performed directly for foreign customers (recipient abroad) and certain offshore goods-related services are also zero-rated under Art. 7/18 LTVA when the recipient's seat or permanent establishment is abroad and the service is actually used abroad. The supplier must hold documentary evidence of the export or offshore nature of the supply; otherwise VAT at 8.1% must be charged.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung / Transit-declaration per e-dec or e-déc), Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR, Inward Remittance Certificate (bank transfer confirmation evidencing foreign payment)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ESTV audits export documentation with high scrutiny. If export proof is missing, incomplete, or false, the previously zero-rated supply is reclassified as taxable in Switzerland, subject to VAT at 8.1% plus default interest (currently 4.75% pa). For fraudulent claims (wilful tax evasion), surcharges up to three times the evaded tax may be imposed, and criminal prosecution under Swiss VAT law may be initiated. Limitation periods: 5 years for ordinary assessment; 10 years for undeclared and fraudulent transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB); no separate foreign exchange administration authority exists in Switzerland.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc (CHF) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. No exchange control restrictions apply. Profit remittances, dividends, royalties and internal capital movements are freely permitted; however, payments that constitute taxable Swiss-sourced income may be subject to Swiss withholding tax at 35% unless reduced under an applicable double tax treaty, and the recipient must provide the necessary tax residence attestation. No profit repatriation licensing or prior approval regime exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland does not impose any statutory timeline for the repatriation or surrender of export proceeds, nor any mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts may be retained in any permitted currency and freely converted into CHF or other currencies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating for offshore digital EMI onboarding: Low. Swiss financial market law requires any entity conducting deposit-taking, payment processing or e-money issuance on a professional basis to obtain a FINMA license (banking licence, FinTech licence, or payment service provider authorisation). Offshore digital EMIs cannot passport EU/EEA licences into Switzerland absent a specific FINMA recognition. A low-risk e-commerce operator may use a regulated Swiss PSP or a FINMA-licensed FinTech service for payment processing. Registration with the Swiss registry of beneficial owners and AML KYC obligations remain mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss AML/CFT due diligence requires reliable identification of the ultimate beneficial owner, board of directors and authorised signatories. Remote video identification is permitted under FINMA Circular 2016/07 for certain low-risk clients, but banks retain discretionary authority to demand physical presence of directors and the ultimate beneficial owner, particularly for non-resident controlled AGs without an established local business track record. A physical presence interview is strongly recommended and may be contractually mandated by individual bank policy for the capital escrow account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) appears on adverse media or is a politically exposed person (PEP)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence package comprising a PEP/UBO explanatory memorandum, tax office clearance certificates, audited source-of-wealth report, source-of-funds evidence, existing bank reference letters, official beneficial ownership register excerpt and a sworn declaration of lawful origin of capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive, fragmented or unexplained third-party payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements, detailed invoice ledger, logistics and carrier proofs, customs declarations, inventory valuation report, VAT filing documentation and a bank-level reconciliation confirming that all payment flows map to commercial underlying transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated AG with complex corporate structure or recent total change in shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organisational chart, notarised share register, capital verification statement from the Swiss Commercial Register, board minutes authorising the banking relationship, lease agreements and material contracts, plus reference letters from previous financial institutions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections from foreign shareholders must be executed via SWIFT MT103 using CHF as the settlement currency. No Swiss foreign-exchange approval or conversion licence is required, but the bank must receive the notarised capital increase resolution, the Commercial Register entry confirming the new capital, and a precise payment purpose reference stating 'Capital increase / share subscription'. The remitter must match the registered shareholder and the declared UBO. Funds may be held in CHF or in permitted foreign currencies, and are subject to standard Swiss AML checks rather than exchange-control authorisation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlement include SWIFT MT103 for priority international wires, SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated payments within the EEA, and documentary letters of credit under ICC UCP 600 for high-value or risk-mitigated supplier settlements. For a low-risk e-commerce buyer paying 3D printer resin and filament suppliers, MT103 transfers with complete beneficiary bank details are operationally most reliable. SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) is available for real-time EUR payments within participating European banks. Disbursements to sanctioned or restricted jurisdictions are prohibited and require mandatory name-screening before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (outright and swap-based)
European-style vanilla FX options (puts and calls)
Deliverable FX swaps for liquidity management
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CHF are legally permissible but non-standard because CHF is freely convertible; availability is at the discretion of the Swiss counterparty bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return Package (Direct Federal Tax, Cantonal and Communal Income Tax, Cantonal Capital Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (e.g., Kantonales Steueramt Zug) and Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV), Berne
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6-8 months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year filers commonly face a 31 August-30 September filing deadline with discretionary canton extension to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 4.5% p.a.; default tax assessment where no return is filed; willful tax evasion surcharge of 0.25x to 3x the evaded federal tax (DBG Art. 175) and equivalent cantonal penalties under StHG.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Return (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA) - Quarterly Period Return or Annual Simplified Small-Taxpayer Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV), VAT Division, Berne
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly: within 60 days after quarter-end (90 days where deferred-payment special arrangement applies); annual simplified return with yearly settlement: by 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on late and under-declared VAT; procedural fines up to CHF 8,000; willful tax evasion surcharge up to 3x the evaded tax plus recovery of shortfall (MWSTG Art. 96-97).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual OASI/AHV Social Security Wage Statement and Definitive Employer Payroll Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (AHV/AVS Ausgleichskasse) for registered place of business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Employee wage certificates (Lohnausweis) by 31 January; consolidated annual OASI/ADL wage declaration for prior-year payroll due by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest at 5% p.a.; board liability for unremitted employee contributions; administrative penalty up to CHF 30,000 for deliberate under-declaration of contributory wages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner (UBO) Register Confirmation and Change Notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Central Office for the Beneficial Owner Register (ZAS) under fedpol; internal protocol maintained in the corporate files
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual re-verification of all qualifying shareholdings (25% or more) at the shareholder meeting; legally binding change notifications to ZAS within 30 days of any transfer or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to CHF 100,000 for willful failure to file UBO changes or for submitting materially false ownership information (VzBoR / nBO Art. 9).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register Mutation Filings (recurring statutory registrations: board changes, capital movements, registered-office moves)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered domicile canton
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the underlying corporate event (e.g., AGM re-election of directors); notarized signature authentication required for each filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compulsory registration order with warning; administrative fine up to CHF 10,000 under OR/HRegV; persistent non-compliance can trigger official dissolution proceedings in the cantonal court with consequential commercial-register strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Full statutory audit (ordentliche Revision) is mandatory when two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years: balance-sheet total above CHF 20 million (approx. USD 25 million), gross turnover above CHF 40 million (approx. USD 50 million), and average headcount above 250 FTE. All other AGs must obtain a limited statutory review (eingeschränkte Revision) by a licensed auditor; companies with fewer than 10 FTE may waive any audit only by unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-963d) with Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS permitted as a recognized substitute for presentation; the statutory financial statements form the binding basis for direct federal tax, cantonal/communal income tax, and capital tax assessments.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The board of directors must maintain an internal register identifying every beneficial owner holding 25% or more of share capital or voting control. At each annual shareholder meeting the register is re-verified against current stock ledgers and any changes in indirect ownership are documented in the minutes. Ownership events altering UBO status must be transmitted to the Federal Central Office within 30 days; the internal register itself remains a non-public corporate record subject to inspection by federal authorities only.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 900-3,000 p.a. / USD 1,000-3,300 p.a. depending on canton (Zug and Zurich premium tier), covering domiciliation address, corporate secretarial handling, mail forwarding, and regulatory mail scanning
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Limited statutory review: CHF 3,000-6,000 / USD 3,300-6,700 for a small e-commerce shelf entity; full statutory audit: CHF 8,000-25,000 / USD 9,000-28,000 depending on transaction volume, 3D-printer inventory valuation, and multi-currency payment-reconciliation complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Swiss Direct Federal Tax (DBG): flat corporate income tax of 8.5% on net profit after federal tax (equivalent to approx. 7.83% expressed on a pre-tax basis); plus cantonal and communal corporate income tax. For an Aktiengesellschaft domiciled in the canton of Zug, the aggregate federal + cantonal + communal statutory burden is approximately 13.5% (Zug effective ordinary tariff, excluding capital tax), depending on the communal multiplier and equity structure.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (STAF, effective 1 January 2020) provides: (i) mandatory patent box regime granting a 90% income relief on qualifying Swiss/EU patent and equivalent IP income, recognized federally and cantonally; (ii) optional R&D super-deduction of up to 50% of qualifying R&D labour costs, capped at 80% of total R&D expenditure (implemented in Zug); (iii) notional interest deduction (NID) on tax-privileged equity in cantons electing this measure; and (iv) participation/substantial relief: dividends and capital gains derived from qualifying participations of at least 10%, held for at least one year, are exempt from taxable income after prorated financing and administration expenses. A Swiss AG engaged in online retail of desktop 3D printers and resin filaments may additionally apply standard commercial depreciation and inventory valuation; no bespoke e-commerce or digital-sector tax holiday exists.
